root_cause.text: vxlan_na_create() in the VXLAN IPv6 ND handling path trusted attacker-controlled ND option length fields without bounding them against the remaining option buffer, leading to out-of-bounds option traversal and possible short-payload reads of the source LLADDR option.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds checks for `!ns->opt[i + 1] || i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) > ns_olen` before advancing through `ns->opt`, and only uses `daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr)` when `(ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) >= sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN`; the CVE/commit message explicitly says malformed options could make the parser "advance beyond the computed option span" or "use a too-short source LLADDR option payload."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds and length validation when parsing Neighbor Solicitation options to prevent malformed ND packets from causing invalid memory access.
intent_record.what: The loop that parses IPv6 Neighbor Solicitation options in vxlan_na_create() was tightened by expanding the existing zero-length option check to also reject an option whose computed length would extend past ns_olen, and by changing the ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR handling so daddr is assigned only if that option's length is at least sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now stops and frees the reply buffer when it encounters malformed ND options with invalid length fields or options that overrun the packet's option area, and it avoids taking a source link-layer address pointer from a too-short ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR option. This prevents out-of-bounds parsing and use of invalid option data from malformed packets.

This dereferences ns->opt[i] during parsing after traversal based on unvalidated option lengths, so malformed lengths can cause this read to occur outside the valid option buffer.

After locating a supposedly matching option via unchecked traversal, this computes a pointer to the source LLADDR payload without verifying that the option is large enough or fully contained in the packet, leading to possible short-payload reads.

The vulnerable construct is present at `1377: for (i = 0; i < ns_olen-1; i += (ns->opt[i+1]<<3)) {`. This loop uses the attacker-controlled ND option length field `ns->opt[i+1]` to advance through the options, but there is no validation that this length is nonzero or that `(i + option_length)` stays within the remaining `ns_olen` buffer. The code only checks `i < ns_olen-1`, which is not enough to ensure safe traversal of variable-length options. It then reads `ns->opt[i]` and, when matching `ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR`, sets `daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr);` at `1379`, again without verifying that the option is large enough to contain a full source LLADDR payload. This matches the root cause: trusting ND option length fields without bounding them against the remaining option buffer, enabling out-of-bounds traversal and short-payload reads. No fix is visible here, such as checking the remaining option space before advancing/reading or validating the source LLADDR option length before using it.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
vxlan: fix nonfunctional neigh_reduce()

The VXLAN neigh_reduce() code is completely non-functional since
check-in. Spec
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is directly present in this function. The code computes the remaining ND options length as `ns_olen = request->len - skb_transport_offset(request) - sizeof(*ns);` and then iterates with `for (i = 0; i < ns_olen-1; i += (ns->opt[i+1]<<3)) {`. This loop trusts the attacker-controlled option length byte `ns->opt[i+1]` as the step size without validating that the option fits within the remaining buffer. There is no check that `(i + 1)` is within bounds before reading `ns->opt[i+1]`, no check that the computed option length is nonzero, and no check that the full option header/body stays within `ns_olen`. When `ns->opt[i] == ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR`, the code sets `daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr);`, again without verifying that the source LLADDR option payload is fully present. This matches the root cause: unbounded traversal of ND options and possible short-payload reads of the source LLADDR option. No corrective bounds validation is present, so the fix is not yet in this version.
